key_insight: FedReLa tackles federated learning under severe class imbalance by re-labeling data to better align local client distributions with the unknown global class distribution. This helps the aggregated model learn more effectively when some classes are missing or rare on many clients.
problem_solved: The paper addresses performance degradation in federated learning caused by the combination of global class imbalance, cross-client data heterogeneity, and severe class absence on individual clients. It targets the challenge of using data-level methods when the true global class distribution is unknown.
method: Re-label local data to reduce mismatch between client-level and global-level class imbalance.
Design the method to remain effective even when some classes are absent on many clients.
Improve the quality of federated aggregation by making local training signals more balanced and informative.
impact: FedReLa offers a practical way to improve federated learning in real-world, non-IID settings where data are unevenly distributed across devices. This can lead to more robust and fairer models for privacy-preserving applications with long-tailed or incomplete class coverage.

paper_title: FedReLa: Imbalanced Federated Learning via Re-Labeling
paper_authors: Guangzheng Hu, Patricia Menéndez, Feng Liu, Mingming Gong, Guanghui Wang
